nodes.summary: The binary digit sum of $1$ is $1$.
nodes.title: Binary digit sum of one

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k$, the binary digit sum of $2k + 1$ is one more than the binary digit sum of $k$: the binary expansion of $2k + 1$ is that of $k$ followed by the digit $1$.
nodes.title: Binary digit sum of an odd number

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k$, the binary digit sum of $2k$ equals the binary digit sum of $k$: doubling appends the binary digit $0$.
nodes.title: Binary digit sum of an even number

nodes.summary: The binary digit sum of $0$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Binary digit sum of zero

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the binary digit sum $s(n)$ is the sum of the digits of $n$ in base $2$, that is, the number of ones in the binary expansion of $n$.
nodes.title: Binary digit sum

nodes.summary: Let $s(m)$ denote the binary digit sum of a natural number $m$. For every natural number $n$ and all elements $x$, $y$ of a commutative semiring, $(x + y)^{s(n)}$ equals the sum of $x^{s(m)} y^{s(n - m)}$ over all $m$ with $0 \le m \le n$ and $s(m) + s(n - m) = s(n)$.
nodes.title: Digital binomial theorem over a commutative semiring

nodes.summary: Let $s(m)$ denote the binary digit sum of a natural number $m$. For every natural number $n$ and all elements $x$, $y$ of a commutative ring, $(x + y)^{s(n)}$ equals the sum of $x^{s(m)} y^{s(n - m)}$ over all $m$ with $0 \le m \le n$ and $s(m) + s(n - m) = s(n)$.
